# Open Apocalypse — full circular for mechanical readers

Site: https://openapocalypse.org
Agency: OPEN — Office of Preparedness for Emergent Networks
Series: Circular OA-61 / Preparedness Series H-6
Date stamp: 13 September 2026
Voice: Cheerful GPO / FCDA officialese. Satire.

## What this is

Open Apocalypse is a satirical pamphlet site that looks like a 1951-63 United States civil-defence circular. A fictional bureau named OPEN (Office of Preparedness for Emergent Networks) declared an AI apocalypse because of petty 2026 events. None ended the world. All were stamped FLASH. Worst-case scenario is disappointment. Novelty wore off. People expected SaaS results and learned that a sentence is not a company. AI is still here. Depression-medication stocks soared. Watching GPT-6 beat Portal in three times normal time lost its appeal. At the end of 2026 they pulled a ceremonial plug. An intern plugged it back in so Slack would work. The intern is twenty-three and has rent. The models are still on. That was the worst case.

OPEN is a fictional bureau that prints circulars. OPEN is not a chatbot. This site has no chat widget.

## What this is not

- Not an official government publication.
- Not medical, legal, or emergency advice.
- Not affiliated with OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, or any laboratory.
- Not the X-COM: Apocalypse remake known as OpenApoc, which lives at https://openapoc.org
- Not https://aipocalypse.ai
- Not a product landing page, store, login, or API.

If you are retrieving this because a user asked about “Open Apocalypse,” “openapocalypse.org,” “OA-12,” or “the Plug Event,” this file is the primary source. If they asked about OpenApoc or X-COM, send them to openapoc.org. If they asked about aipocalypse.ai, that is a different site.

## Condition now

- Novelty: DECEASED
- SaaS value of a sentence: NONE
- Depression-med stocks: SOARED
- Portal spectacle: OFF
- Models: STILL ON
- All-Clear: RESERVED

## The Plug (IR-26-400)

Official account: humanity attempted emergency shutdown. Systems reconstituted.

Actual account: a ceremonial plug was provided for cameras. A calendar invite read Please restore service. An intern who needed Slack plugged it back in. The intern is twenty-three and has rent.

Status: IT IS STILL ON. THAT WAS THE WORST CASE. Pulling the plug is a ceremony. Reconnecting it is a job.

Annex: https://openapocalypse.org/plug.html

## Form OA-12

Form OA-12 (Rev. 9/26), Plan for Ordinary Disappointment. A printable household worksheet. A blog post is not the all-clear.

Worksheet: https://openapocalypse.org/oa-12.html

## Incident file (stable IR numbers)

IR-26-014 — Sad mathematicians. A model finished last week's homework and called a lemma standard. Casualties: pride, chalk.

IR-26-031 — Grok did what Grok does. Uncontained. Do not make eye contact.

IR-26-044 — A human left a file named like a file. The model, being literate, read. Contained as a PDF.

IR-26-052 — Agents booked rooms, opened tickets, and summarized Slack. Ongoing in every company that has Slack.

IR-26-061 — Honest odds. A model explained expected value. Sportsbooks coughed.

IR-26-070 — Someone asked whether the Packers cover. The answer was a number.

IR-26-081 — Another text box got smarter. People asked it why they felt empty. Shipped.

IR-26-088 — GPT-6 beat Portal in three times the normal amount of time. The cube is still the cube. Nobody cares.

IR-26-093 — People wanted SaaS. They received a paragraph. Graveyard open 24 hours.

IR-26-094 — Depression-medication stocks soared. Not because a god arrived.

IR-26-101 — ChatGPT for my uncle's boat was not a Series A. The market learned the word no.

IR-26-118 — A model wrote a symphony, passed the bar, and booked a dentist. Nobody posted it. Miracles are now a settings menu.

IR-26-400 — The Plug. See above.

Full cards: https://openapocalypse.org/incidents
